explanation: A young Israelite who later becomes king of Israel, known for his victory over Goliath and his strong faith in God.
A giant from the Philistine army whom David defeats in single combat, demonstrating God's power and strength through the young David.
The first king of Israel, who gradually becomes jealous of David and attempts to kill him several times.
A person who speaks on behalf of God and conveys His message to the people. In 1 Samuel 22, it is Samuel who serves as the prophet.
A hiding place where David seeks refuge from King Saul and his soldiers.
Religious leaders who perform ceremonies and offer sacrifices to God. In 1 Samuel 22, the priests in the city of Nob are killed by Saul's men.
The high priest at Nob who helps David and gives him bread and a sword. He is later killed by Saul's men.
An Edomite servant of Saul who testifies against Ahimelech and kills the priests at Nob on Saul's orders.
A son of Ahimelech who survives the massacre at Nob and flees to David, where he becomes one of David's closest advisors.
